explicit_validation.explanation: Both LLM (GPT-4 for informativeness, GPT-2 for fluency) and human (hallucination annotations) evaluations are conducted, but they assess different criteria on different sets of instances with no quantitative comparison or validation between the two methods

prompts.notes: No prompts or detailed descriptions of LLM evaluation methodology are provided beyond stating GPT-4 is used for informativeness assessment and GPT-2 for fluency scoring via perplexity

guidelines.notes: Guidelines mention annotators label each object in generated captions as hallucinated or non-hallucinated and determine whether overall response contains hallucinations, but no detailed rubric or examples shown

criteria_mapping.notes: LLM and human evaluations focus on completely different aspects - LLM assesses generation quality (informativeness, fluency) while human evaluation focuses exclusively on hallucination detection
